I found one well-supported generalisation, reported below.

Other points I considered and left out:

- I did not report the `∀ B M` quantification in `hMC`. It is consumed downstream in exactly this form, and `finiteMcDiarmidInput` discharges it in every case, so specialising it gives no practical gain.

Remaining uncertainty: I could not run Lean, so the proposed proof has not been compiled. It only rearranges terms whose signatures I read, and RationalThresholds.lean, which the target already imports, provides every lemma it needs.

findings.problem: All four theorems take the quantitative KMT bound `hKMT : CharacterDistanceInput`, but their proofs only use its consequence `CharacterDistanceDivergence`. The chain goes through `rationalFixedScaleLaw_of_published`, which applies `characterDistanceDivergence_of_published hKMT` immediately and passes the result to `rationalFixedScaleLaw_of_distance_divergence`. The weaker qualitative statement is proved unconditionally in the library (`characterDistanceDivergence`). Even so, the conditional main theorems cannot take it. DischargedMain therefore has to bypass `main_results_of_published`. `main_results_after_character_distance` and `main_results_after_exponential_sums` each re-derive the joint law and both ordering laws by inlining `jointDickmanLaw_of_rational_fixedScale (rationalFixedScaleLaw_of_distance_divergence ...)` and the two ordering lemmas.
findings.proposed_change:
Change the section binder to `(hKMT : CharacterDistanceDivergence)`; this file opens `JointDickman`, so the name resolves. Prove the first theorem as
`theorem jointDickmanLaw_of_published : JointDickmanLaw :=
  jointDickmanLaw_of_rational_fixedScale
    (rationalFixedScaleLaw_of_distance_divergence hMR hMRT hKMT hFord hSD hSW hM hMP hMC hBill)`
The other three theorems stay as they are. If a version stated with the published KMT input is still wanted, add a one-line corollary `main_results_of_published' ... (hKMT : CharacterDistanceInput) := main_results_of_published hMR hMRT (characterDistanceDivergence_of_published hKMT) ...`. Alternatively, update `main_results_after_mertens` to pass `characterDistanceDivergence_of_published hKMT`. In DischargedMain, `main_results_after_character_distance` and `main_results_after_exponential_sums` could then be one-liners: `main_results_of_published hMR hMRT characterDistanceDivergence fordUpperSieveInput ... finiteBinDistributionInput`. All hypotheses are Props, so there is no degenerate case to handle. The only elaboration dependency is `rationalFixedScaleLaw_of_distance_divergence`, which is defined in the already-imported RationalThresholds.lean with exactly this argument order.
findings.benefit: The conditional main theorem would be stated under the hypothesis it actually needs. Users could instantiate it directly with the proved `characterDistanceDivergence` rather than a stronger numerical bound they may not have. It would also remove the duplicated proof chains in DischargedMain, and the 'progressively weaker hypotheses' sequence there could reuse the main results rather than re-proving them.
